# Revised Form {.unnumbered}

::: {style="border-left:6px solid #0b6e99;background:#eaf4f9;padding:14px 18px;border-radius:6px;"}

<p class="chapter-lead">Health Facility Registration Form<br>Proposed revised version, with questions written out in full and HHFA indicators annotated</p>

Working version for discussion with the Office of Studies, Planning and Statistics. It keeps the structure, the numbering and the purpose of Form version 19_01, and reformulates the questions and the response options following the wording of the Harmonized Health Facility Assessment, translated from the original.

**Every question is written out in full, exactly as it is to be read aloud**, with the unit of measure, the reference period and the point of reference built into the text itself. **Each one is annotated with the HHFA indicator that it makes computable.**

:::

::: {style="border:3px solid #c0392b;background:#fdecea;padding:18px 20px;border-radius:8px;margin:18px 0;"}

### ⚠ READ FIRST: the drafting standard adopted

<p style="font-size:1.08em;line-height:1.55;margin:0 0 10px 0;"><strong style="color:#c0392b;">A question that each enumerator has to complete on their own is a different question in every health facility.</strong> "Distance to the referral facility — minutes, total km" forces the person collecting the data to decide alone which road, by which means of transport, in which season of the year, and measured how. The answers that come out of it are not comparable with one another, and no subsequent analysis can recover that variation.</p>

<p style="font-size:1.04em;line-height:1.5;margin:0 0 10px 0;">This version applies nine drafting rules to every question. They are the same ones the HHFA applies, and the effect is that the question stays identical across all facilities, whoever asks it.</p>

<ol style="font-size:1.0em;line-height:1.5;margin:0 0 12px 0;">
<li><strong>The question is read out in full, exactly as written.</strong> The enumerator neither completes nor summarises it.</li>
<li><strong>The unit of measure is inside the question</strong> — kilometres, minutes, number of people, square metres.</li>
<li><strong>The reference period is inside the question</strong> — today, in the past 7 days, in the past 3 months, in the past 12 months, in the past 2 years.</li>
<li><strong>The point of reference is inside the question</strong> — from where to where, counted how, by whom, under what conditions.</li>
<li><strong>One question yields one fact.</strong> Composite concepts are split into separate questions.</li>
<li><strong>The response options are mutually exclusive and exhaustive</strong>, and they are written on the form, not left to the judgement of whoever is recording the answer.</li>
<li><strong>There is always a code for "does not know"</strong> (98) and, where applicable, for "not applicable" (97). A blank field is no longer ambiguous.</li>
<li><strong>Instructions to the enumerator are set apart graphically</strong> from the text to be read to the respondent. In this document they appear in <em>italics and in capitals</em>.</li>
<li><strong>Consistency checks are stated</strong> alongside the questions they apply to, so that they can be programmed into the data collection application.</li>
</ol>

<hr style="border:none;border-top:2px dashed #c0392b;margin:14px 0;">

<p style="font-size:1.03em;line-height:1.5;margin:0 0 8px 0;"><strong style="color:#c0392b;">The HHFA foresees instruments exactly like the Health Map.</strong> The inventory has two subareas — <strong>1.3.2, availability of specific services</strong>, and <strong>1.3.3, availability of technologies and procedures</strong> — whose titles end with the note <em>"to be used only when the readiness module does not apply"</em>. This proposal rests on that route, and the consequence is highly favourable: <strong>more than nine in ten of the indicators captured here yield in self-reported mode</strong>, requiring neither observation nor any change to the current collection process.</p>

<p style="font-size:1.0em;line-height:1.45;margin:0;"><strong>Conventions.</strong> The numbering of existing items is retained, so that the historical series can be reconstructed. <strong>[MS]</strong> marks items specific to the Health Map, with no counterpart in the HHFA, which are kept because they are its own particular contribution — but <strong>they too are reformulated</strong>, because the drafting problem is independent of where the question came from. <strong>◆</strong> marks the questions that require an enumerator making observations. The lists so flagged still need validation by the national programmes.</p>

:::

---

## SECTION 0 — Identification of the data collection

**0.1** Date on which this form was completed: |\_\_|\_\_| day · |\_\_|\_\_| month · |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| year

**0.2** **How was this form completed?**
*READ THE OPTIONS.*
> 1 Completed by the facility staff and sent to GEPE, with no enumerator visit
> 2 Completed by an enumerator during a visit to the facility
> 3 Completed by the facility staff and then checked by an enumerator during a visit

*Indicator: essential metadata. Without it, the analysis cannot separate what was verified from what was merely declared.*

**0.3** **What is the position of the person who answered most of this form?**
> 1 Facility director · 2 Deputy director · 3 Head of nursing · 4 Head of administration · 5 Head of statistics · 6 Other position (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_

**0.4** **Does this facility have a budget of its own — that is, an allocation of funds assigned specifically to this facility, which its management can administer and execute?**
*DO NOT COUNT FUNDS MANAGED ENTIRELY BY THE MUNICIPAL OR PROVINCIAL DIRECTORATE ON THE FACILITY'S BEHALF.*
> 1 Yes · 2 No · 98 Does not know

*HHFA indicator: **4.2.1.1.1** (anchor — see note).*

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**Note on 0.4.** In the current Form, item 0.2 says only "Tick if the facility has its OWN BUDGET", without defining what counts as such. A director who receives a municipal allocation earmarked for their facility and a director who runs a bank account of their own both answer "yes", and these are administratively very different situations. The wording above fixes the criterion — **the power to administer and execute** — and explicitly excludes the ambiguous case. HHFA indicator 4.2.1.1.1 is more demanding still (autonomy to manage a bank account of one's own); it is proposed that the public financial management group decide which of the two criteria serves Angola better, and that it be fixed in the question.

:::

## SECTION 1 — Location

**1.1 to 1.5** Province · Municipality · Commune or urban district · Rural village or urban neighbourhood · Name of the health facility
*RECORD THE NAME AND THE CODE GIVEN BY THE HEALTH MAP.*

**1.6** Category of the facility, according to the Health Map classification
*THE PRINCIPAL STRATIFIER FOR ALL ANALYSIS. It is the national list of facility types that replaces the generic HHFA list.*

**1.7 and 1.8** **Reading of the geographic coordinates.**
*TAKE THE READING AT THE MAIN ENTRANCE OF THE MAIN BUILDING, IN THE OPEN AIR, WITH THE DEVICE HELD STEADY FOR AT LEAST 60 SECONDS. RECORD IN DECIMAL DEGREES, TO FIVE DECIMAL PLACES.*
> 1.7 Latitude: |\_\_|\_\_|.|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|
> 1.8 Longitude: |\_\_|\_\_|.|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|
> 1.8.1 Accuracy shown by the device, in metres: |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|

**1.9** **Is this health facility located in an urban, a rural or a peri-urban area?**
*USE THE ADMINISTRATIVE CLASSIFICATION IN FORCE. IF IN DOUBT, ASK THE RESPONDENT.*
> 1 Urban · 2 Rural · 3 Peri-urban

*Allows urban/rural disaggregation of every indicator in this form.*

## SECTION 2 — Ownership and management

**2.1** **Who owns this health facility?**
*MARK ONE OPTION ONLY.*
> 1 Public — National Health Service · 2 Public — Police or Armed Forces · 3 Private not-for-profit (religious denomination, non-governmental organization, association) · 4 Private for-profit · 96 Other situation (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_

**2.2** **Which entity is responsible for the day-to-day management of this facility — that is, who appoints the management and answers for its daily operation?**
*THIS MAY DIFFER FROM THE OWNER RECORDED IN 2.1.*
> 1 Public · 2 Private · 3 Mixed · 96 Other situation (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_

## SECTION 3 — Catchment population and referral system

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #1e8449;background:#eafaf1;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**Why this section matters more than it appears to.** The catchment population is the denominator of the densities. Crossed with the staff count in Section 11 and with the beds in Section 8, it yields on its own twenty-three system-level indicators — the kind of figure that underpins resource allocation decisions and that no sample survey can deliver with national coverage.

:::

### 3.1 Catchment population

**3.1** **What is the total resident population in the catchment area of this health facility, according to the most recent estimate available to the facility?**
*RECORD THE NUMBER OF INHABITANTS. RECORD 999998 IF THE FACILITY HAS NO ESTIMATE.*
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| inhabitants

*HHFA indicators: **1.1.1.1.1 to 1.1.1.1.4** (facility and bed density), **1.2.2.1.1 to 1.2.2.4.8** (health worker density per 10,000 population), **1.4.1.1.1 to 1.4.1.1.3** (density scores).*

**3.1.1** **Where does that population estimate come from?**
> 1 National census · 2 Projection by the National Institute of Statistics · 3 Registration or enumeration carried out by the facility itself · 4 Estimate provided by the Municipal Health Directorate · 5 Estimate provided by the Provincial Health Directorate · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_ · 98 Does not know

**3.1.2** **Which year does that estimate refer to?** |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**Why these two questions.** In the current Form, 3.1 asks for the catchment population "if known", and nothing more. A 2014 census estimate and a head count made by the facility itself last year go into the same field and produce densities that cannot be compared. Two short questions qualify the denominator and make it possible, at the analysis stage, to decide which estimates to use.

:::

### 3.2 Referral facility

**3.2.1** **To which health facility are patients from this facility usually transferred when they need care that cannot be provided here?**
*IF THERE IS MORE THAN ONE, GIVE THE ONE TO WHICH THE LARGEST NUMBER OF PATIENTS WAS TRANSFERRED IN THE PAST 12 MONTHS.*
> Name of the facility: \_\_\_\_\_\_ · Health Map code: |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|

**3.2.2** Category of that referral facility, according to the Health Map classification: |\_\_|\_\_|

**3.2.3** **What is the means of transport most frequently used to transfer patients from this facility to the facility named in 3.2.1?**
*CONSIDER THE PAST 12 MONTHS. MARK ONE OPTION ONLY.*
> 1 Ambulance belonging to this facility · 2 Ambulance from another facility or from the Municipal Directorate · 3 Light vehicle belonging to the facility · 4 Motorcycle · 5 Public or private transport, paid for by the patient or the family · 6 On foot or by stretcher · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_

**3.2.4** **Considering the route usually taken by that means of transport, what is the total distance, in kilometres, between this health facility and the referral facility?**
*DISTANCE ALONG THE ROAD ACTUALLY TRAVELLED, NOT IN A STRAIGHT LINE. RECORD 998 IF NOT KNOWN.*
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| kilometres

**3.2.5** **Of that route, how many kilometres are on paved road?**
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| kilometres

**3.2.6** **And how many kilometres are on dirt road or dirt track?**
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| kilometres

*CONSISTENCY CHECK: 3.2.5 + 3.2.6 must equal 3.2.4. IF IT DOES NOT, CONFIRM WITH THE RESPONDENT BEFORE CONTINUING.*

**3.2.7** **In the dry season, how long does that route usually take, in minutes, by the means of transport given in 3.2.3?**
*TRAVEL TIME ONLY, NOT COUNTING TIME SPENT WAITING FOR TRANSPORT. RECORD 998 IF NOT KNOWN.*
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| minutes

**3.2.8** **And in the rainy season, how long does the same route usually take, in minutes?**
*RECORD 997 IF THE ROUTE BECOMES IMPASSABLE AT ANY POINT DURING THE RAINY SEASON. RECORD 998 IF NOT KNOWN.*
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| minutes

*Indicators: **[MS]**. Crossed with 2.1.1.1.7 (emergency transport), they make it possible to identify the areas where obstetric evacuation cannot be achieved within a useful time.*

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**What has changed, and why.** The current Form has an item 3.2.3 with four fields — minutes, total km, km of paved road, km of dirt track — and no instruction at all. Nothing says which road is to be measured, in which means of transport the minutes are counted, whether the time includes waiting for the ambulance, or what to do when the dirt track becomes impassable in the rains. Three enumerators produce three different answers for the same facility, and the difference between them is indistinguishable from the real difference between facilities.

The six questions above fix: **the means of transport** (3.2.3, which becomes a datum with value in its own right — a facility that evacuates on foot is a different reality), **the road actually travelled** rather than the straight line, **the breakdown verified by addition**, and **the two seasons of the year**, with a code of its own for the impassable route. It becomes possible to calculate evacuation time in the worst season, which is the information that matters for maternal mortality.

:::

### 3.3 Functioning of the referral system

**3.3** **Does this facility have an established system for referring patients to other health facilities?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No · 98 Does not know

*HHFA indicator: **2.7.1.1.1**.*

**3.4 ◆** **Are there written guidelines or protocols in this facility that guide the referral of patients to other facilities?**
*IF YES, ASK TO SEE THE DOCUMENT.*
> 1 Yes, observed · 2 Yes, reported but not seen · 3 Not available

*HHFA indicator: **2.7.1.1.2** (only option 1 counts).*

**3.5 ◆** **And are there written guidelines or protocols for back-referral — that is, for the patient's return to this facility after being seen at the referral facility?**
*IF YES, ASK TO SEE THE DOCUMENT.*
> 1 Yes, observed · 2 Yes, reported but not seen · 3 Not available

*HHFA indicator: **2.7.1.1.3**.*

**3.6 ◆** **Does this facility keep a record, in a register book or in a file, of the patients it has referred to other facilities?**
*IF YES, ASK TO SEE THE RECORD.*
> 1 Yes, observed · 2 Yes, reported but not seen · 3 Keeps no record

*HHFA indicator: **2.7.1.1.4**.*

**3.7** **In the past 3 months, has this facility received clinical information back about patients it had referred — in writing or by any other means?**
> 1 Yes, about most of the patients referred · 2 Yes, about some patients · 3 Received no information back · 97 Referred no patients in the past 3 months · 98 Does not know

*HHFA indicator: **2.7.1.1.5** (options 1 and 2 count).*

**3.8** **Does this facility have access, 24 hours a day and every day of the week, to a vehicle in working order and to a driver available to transport patients?**
*THE VEHICLE MAY BE STATIONED AT THIS FACILITY OR BE CALLED IN FROM ELSEWHERE.*
> 1 Yes · 2 No · 98 Does not know

*HHFA indicator: **2.7.1.1.6**.*

## SECTION 4 — Buildings and construction

**[MS] — A section specific to the Health Map.** The HHFA collects none of this information, and it is the basis of decisions on construction works. It is retained in full, with the wording made precise.

**4.1** **How many buildings, in total, make up this health facility?**
*COUNT ALL BUILDINGS WITHIN THE GROUNDS THAT ARE USED BY THE FACILITY, INCLUDING SUPPORT BUILDINGS — STORE, KITCHEN, LAUNDRY, MORTUARY. DO NOT COUNT STAFF HOUSING, WHICH IS COUNTED IN 4.3. DO NOT COUNT BUILDINGS IN RUINS OR WITH NO USE AT ALL.*
> |\_\_|\_\_| buildings

**4.2** **What is the total covered floor area of those buildings, in square metres?**
*ADD UP THE COVERED AREA OF ALL THE BUILDINGS COUNTED IN 4.1. RECORD 9998 IF NOT KNOWN.*
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| m²

**4.3** **How many staff houses are there within the grounds of this facility or under its responsibility?**
> |\_\_|\_\_| houses

**4.4** **What is the total covered floor area of those houses, in square metres?**
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| m²

**4.5** **In which year was construction of the main building of this facility completed?**
*IF IT HAS BEEN SUBSTANTIALLY REBUILT, GIVE THE YEAR OF THE REBUILDING. RECORD 9998 IF NOT KNOWN.*
> |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|

**4.6** **In which period was the main building constructed?**
*READ THE OPTIONS. THIS SERVES TO CLASSIFY THE CASES IN WHICH THE EXACT YEAR IS NOT KNOWN.*
> 1 Before 1975 · 2 Between 1975 and 1991 · 3 Between 1992 and 2002 · 4 Between 2003 and 2012 · 5 From 2013 onwards · 98 Does not know

**4.7** **What is the predominant material of the exterior walls of the main building?**
*MARK ONE OPTION ONLY — THE MATERIAL COVERING MOST OF THE WALL SURFACE.*
> 1 Cement blocks · 2 Fired brick · 3 Adobe or mud brick · 4 Wattle and daub or timber · 5 Metal sheeting · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_

---

## SECTION 5 — State of repair

**[MS] — A section specific to the Health Map.** It is retained with the construction criteria from the Filling Guide, now made explicit in the question itself.

**5.1** **Considering the foundations, the structure, the flooring, the walls, the roof, the false ceiling and the sanitary installations of the main building, which of the following situations best describes its current state?**
*READ ALL THE OPTIONS BEFORE MARKING. APPLY THE DETAILED CRITERIA IN THE FILLING GUIDE. MARK ONE OPTION ONLY.*
> 1 Needs no intervention — all elements in good condition
> 2 Needs routine maintenance — minor repairs, painting, occasional replacements
> 3 Needs rehabilitation — one or more elements degraded, but the structure is sound
> 4 Needs reconstruction — structure compromised or building unusable

**5.2** **What is the covered floor area, in square metres, that is in each of the following states?**
*THE SUM MUST EQUAL THE TOTAL FLOOR AREA GIVEN IN 4.2.*
> 5.2.1 In good condition: |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| m²
> 5.2.2 Needing routine maintenance: |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| m²
> 5.2.3 Needing rehabilitation: |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| m²
> 5.2.4 Needing reconstruction: |\_\_|\_\_|\_\_|\_\_| m²

*CONSISTENCY CHECK: 5.2.1 + 5.2.2 + 5.2.3 + 5.2.4 must equal 4.2.*

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**What has changed.** In the current Form, 5.2 is a free-text field. Four numeric fields with a sum check make the information directly usable for costing the works, which is the purpose the Filling Guide declares for this item — and they oblige whoever completes the form to apportion the area, rather than write a sentence.

:::

## SECTION 6 — Water, energy, sanitation and waste

### 6.1 Water

**6.1** **What is the water source most used by this health facility at present?**
*READ THE OPTIONS. MARK ONE ONLY. IF THE ANSWER DIFFERS BETWEEN INPATIENT CARE AND OUTPATIENT CARE, GIVE THE ONE FOR INPATIENT CARE.*
> 01 Piped into the building · 02 Piped into the facility grounds · 03 Public tap or standpipe · 04 Borehole · 05 Protected dug well · 06 Unprotected dug well · 07 Protected spring · 08 Unprotected spring · 09 Rainwater · 10 Bottled water · 11 Cart with small tank · 12 Tanker truck · 13 Surface water — river, dam, lake or pond · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_ · 00 Has no water source at all · 98 Does not know

**6.1.2** **Besides that one, what other water sources does this facility use when the main source is not available?**
*MARK ALL THAT APPLY, USING THE SAME CODES AS IN 6.1. RECORD 00 IF THERE IS NO ALTERNATIVE SOURCE.*

*Indicator: **[MS]** — the HHFA does not collect secondary water sources. This is a contribution specific to the Health Map.*

**6.2 ◆** **Is water from that source available within the facility grounds — inside the building or inside the grounds?**
*IF YES, ASK: may I see the water that is available today? If it is inside the building, show me there; otherwise, show me in the grounds. THE WATER MAY BE PIPED OR IN A CONTAINER.*
> 1 Yes, observed inside the building · 2 Yes, observed in the facility grounds · 3 Yes, reported but not seen · 4 No, or available only outside the grounds

*HHFA indicator: **2.1.1.1.2** — improved water source = 6.1 in an improved category **and** 6.2 other than 3 and 4.*

**6.3** **In the past 30 days, was there any period in which this facility was without water and this forced it to suspend or limit the provision of services?**
> 1 There was no such period · 2 Yes, less than a week in total · 3 Yes, a week or more in total · 98 Does not know

### 6.2 Energy

**6.4** **Does this facility have electricity from any source — public grid, generator, solar power or other — including electricity that powers only stand-alone appliances, such as those of the Expanded Programme on Immunization cold chain?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No

*IF 2, GO TO 6.7.*

**6.5** **What is the electricity source most used by this facility?**
*MARK ONE OPTION ONLY.*
> 1 Public grid · 2 Facility generator · 3 Solar panels · 4 Grid of a neighbouring institution · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_

**6.5.1** **What back-up sources are there, for the periods when the main source fails?**
*MARK ALL THAT APPLY. RECORD 00 IF THERE IS NO BACK-UP SOURCE.*
> 1 Public grid · 2 Generator · 3 Solar panels · 4 Batteries · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_ · 00 Has no back-up source

**6.6** **In the past 7 days, was there electricity — from the main source or from any back-up source — at all times when this facility was open to the public?**
*READ ALL THREE OPTIONS.*
> 1 Always available, with no interruptions
> 2 Often available, with interruptions of less than 2 hours a day
> 3 Sometimes available, with frequent interruptions or interruptions of more than 2 hours a day

*HHFA indicator: **2.1.1.1.1** — facilities with power = 6.4 equal to 1 **and** 6.6 equal to 1 or 2.*

### 6.3 Sanitation

**6.7** **Is there a toilet or latrine within the grounds of this facility that can be used by outpatient department users or by staff?**
*IF YES, ASK: what type is it? May I see it? IF THERE ARE SEVERAL, CONSIDER THE MOST MODERN TYPE.*
> Flush toilet connected to: 1 sewer system · 2 septic tank · 3 open or unknown outlet
> 4 Ventilated improved pit latrine · 5 Pit latrine with slab · 6 Composting latrine · 7 Open pit latrine, without slab · 8 Bucket · 9 Hanging toilet · 10 There is no toilet or latrine within the grounds

*HHFA indicator: **2.1.1.1.3** — improved sanitation = options 1, 2, 4 or 6.*

### 6.4 Waste

**6.8** **How is the general waste of this facility collected?**
> 1 By the municipal administrative services · 2 By a contracted company · 3 By the facility itself · 4 There is no organized collection · 98 Does not know

*Indicator: **[MS]**.*

**6.9** **What is the final destination of the sharps waste produced in this facility — needles, blades, broken ampoules?**
*MARK ONE OPTION ONLY — THE DESTINATION OF MOST OF THIS WASTE.*
> 1 Collected and treated off site · 2 Incinerated at this facility · 3 Burned in the open · 4 Buried in a protected pit · 5 Dumped without any treatment · 96 Other (specify) \_\_\_\_\_\_ · 98 Does not know

*HHFA indicator: **2.5.1.1.12** (with 6.11 and 6.12).*

**6.10** **And what is the final destination of non-sharp infectious waste — dressings, gauze, used gloves, contaminated materials?**
*SAME OPTIONS AS 6.9.*

*HHFA indicator: **2.5.1.1.13** (with 6.11 and 6.12).*

**6.11 ◆** **Was the incinerator or other waste treatment facility of this facility working today?**
*ASK TO SEE IT. IF THE DESTINATION GIVEN IN 6.9 AND 6.10 DOES NOT INVOLVE TREATMENT AT THE FACILITY, RECORD 97.*
> 1 Yes, observed working · 2 Was not working · 97 Not applicable · 98 Does not know

**6.12 ◆** **Was fuel available for the incinerator today?**
> 1 Yes, observed · 2 No · 97 Not applicable · 98 Does not know

**6.13** **Are there written guidelines or standard operating procedures on health care waste management in this facility?**
*IF YES, ASK TO SEE THEM.*
> 1 Yes, observed · 2 Yes, reported but not seen · 3 There are none

*HHFA indicator: **2.5.1.1.2**.*

**6.14** **In the past 2 years, has any health worker currently working in this facility received training in health care waste management?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No · 98 Does not know

*HHFA indicator: **2.5.1.1.4**.*

**6.15** **Is there a wastewater treatment plant or system in this facility?**
> 1 Yes, and it was working in the past 30 days · 2 Yes, but it was not working in the past 30 days · 3 There is none

*Indicator: **[MS]**.*

## SECTION 7 — Services

The central section of the Form. It rests on subareas **1.3.2** and **1.3.3** of the HHFA — the ones the instrument reserves for measuring availability without a readiness module.

**A note on reading this section.** Two formats are used here. Stand-alone questions are written out in full. Lists of items — vaccines, tests, contraceptive methods — are set out in a table, which is the HHFA's own format: **the lead-in is read once, in full, and then the items are read one by one**. It is an efficient format provided the lead-in is complete, and that is why all the lead-ins below are written out in full.

### 7.0 Gateway questions

**7.0.1** **Does this facility provide outpatient care — that is, care for patients who are seen and return home the same day?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No

*HHFA indicator: **1.3.1.1.1**.*

**7.0.2** **Does this facility provide inpatient care — that is, care for patients who stay overnight at the facility?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No

*HHFA indicator: **1.3.1.1.2**.*

**7.0.3** **On a normal weekday, for how many hours is the outpatient department of this facility open to the public?**
*COUNT ONLY THE HOURS DURING WHICH PATIENTS ARE ATTENDED TO. IF CARE IS PROVIDED CONTINUOUSLY 24 HOURS, RECORD 24.*
> |\_\_|\_\_| hours

**7.0.4** **And on how many days a week is the outpatient department open to the public?**
> |\_\_| days

*HHFA indicators: **1.3.1.2.1 to 1.3.1.2.4**, **1.3.1.3.1**, **1.3.1.3.2**.*

### 7.1 Clinical and surgical services

**7.1.1 to 7.1.28 — List of specialties.**

*LEAD-IN TO BE READ: "I am going to read out a list of clinical specialties. For each one, tell me whether this facility has a regular clinic in that specialty — that is, on a set day or days of the week — delivered by a qualified health worker. Do not count occasional consultations or clinics that have been suspended for more than 3 months."*
> For each specialty: 1 Yes, regular clinic · 2 No

*Indicator: **[MS]** — the list of 28 specialties is a contribution specific to the Health Map. The lead-in above fixes the criterion ("regular clinic, on a set day, by a qualified health worker") that is today left to the judgement of the respondent.*

**7.1.29** **Does this facility carry out any surgical procedure, minor or major?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No — *IF 2, GO TO 7.2.*

*HHFA indicator: **1.3.2.7.1**.*

**7.1.29.1** **Does this facility carry out minor surgical procedures — that is, procedures performed under local anaesthesia, without the need for an operating theatre?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No — *Indicator: **1.3.2.7.2***

**7.1.29.2** **Does this facility carry out major surgical procedures — that is, procedures performed under general or regional anaesthesia, in an operating theatre?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No — *Indicator: **1.3.2.7.3***

**7.1.29.3** **Does this facility carry out voluntary medical male circumcision?**
> 1 Yes · 2 No — *Indicator: **1.3.2.7.4***

**7.1.29.4** **Of the following three procedures, which have been carried out in this facility in the past 12 months?**
*READ ALL THREE. MARK EACH ONE.*
> a) Caesarean section: 1 Yes · 2 No
> b) Laparotomy: 1 Yes · 2 No
> c) Treatment of open fracture: 1 Yes · 2 No

*HHFA indicators: **1.3.2.7.5** (any of the three) and **1.3.2.7.6** (all three).*

**7.1.30 to 7.1.34** **Does this facility carry out surgical procedures in any of the following specialty areas?**
> Paediatric surgery · Maxillofacial surgery · Vascular surgery · Neurosurgery · Plastic surgery — *1 Yes · 2 No, for each*

*HHFA indicator: **1.3.2.7.7**.*

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**About the marker procedures.** Caesarean section, laparotomy and treatment of open fracture are the three procedures that global surgery uses as markers of essential surgical capacity — they cover obstetrics, the abdomen and trauma. Three questions with a stated reference period say more about actual surgical capacity than the list of specialties does, and the two pieces of information do not exclude each other.

:::

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**The concrete gain, and the reason for the third response option.** Today, ticking BEmONC is a judgement call by whoever fills in the Form. With these twenty lines, BEmONC and CEmONC become **computed results**, and it becomes known *which* function is missing in each facility — the information that makes action possible. Option 2, "practised here but no recent cases", exists because in a small facility a quarter can pass without a single manual removal of the placenta without this meaning any lack of capacity. Without that option, the respondent is forced to choose between two wrong answers.

:::

::: {style="border-left:5px solid #b7950b;background:#fdf6e3;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:5px;"}

**Why the closing instruction in the lead-in is essential.** Without it, a respondent at a health centre with no endocrinologist answers "no" to diabetes, even though diabetes is diagnosed and treated there every day. The instruction "answer according to what the facility does in practice, and not according to whether there is a specialist clinic" is what sets this question apart from the "9. Endocrinology" box of the current Form — and it is what makes the data useful for planning the decentralization of chronic disease management.

:::

## What this version delivers, and what it leaves for later

**345 HHFA indicators**, out of the 2,604 in the inventory. The number on its own says less than its composition does: **nineteen subareas are completed in full**, and they are precisely the availability subareas — what the Health Map Form was designed for. The instrument now produces, in internationally comparable language, exactly what it already set out to measure.

**More than nine in ten yield in self-reported mode.** Only Section 9 requires observation throughout, and it can be applied only in the facilities that are visited without the form ceasing to work in the others.

**The greater gain, however, is not in the number of indicators.** It is in the drafting. A question written out in full, with the unit, the period and the point of reference inside it, produces the same answer whoever asks it — and that is what makes two facilities, two provinces and two editions of the Health Map comparable. Several items in this form add no new indicator and are kept here for that reason alone: the distance to the referral facility, the state of repair, the vehicle fleet, the specialties, the general services. They are **[MS]**, they are the Health Map's own contribution, and they gain in precision without changing their purpose.

**Three items are deliberately left unresolved**, and it is worth saying so: the pharmacy (7.2.10), sterilization and the distribution of albendazole remain as questions about existence. In all three cases the corresponding HHFA indicator depends on physical verification — medicine within its expiry date, equipment working, product observed — and there is no honest way of producing it in self-reported mode. They stay as they are until the decision on observation is taken.

**What is left for the next phase** is the readiness dimension: guidelines available, staff trained, medicines and diagnostic means verified. These are the Type 3 and Type 4 increments in document 4, and they all require an enumerator making observations. They are left out of this version not because they matter less — in many cases they matter more — but because adopting them depends on a decision about the mode of collection that has not yet been taken.

:::
